div.l: Whan þᵗat Aprill wᵗith his shoures soote
The drouȝht of march hath perced to þe rote
And bathed euery vein in swith licoure
Of which vertue engendred is þe floure
Whan zephirus eke with his swete breth
Inspired hath in euerie holt ⁊and heth
The tendir croppis ⁊and þe yonge sonne
Hath in the ram his halfe cours yronne
And smale fowlis make melodye
That slepen all nyght with open eyghe
So priker hem nature / in here corages
Than longen folke to gon in pilgrymages
And palmers for to seke straunge strondes
To ferne halowes couthe in sondry londes
And specially fram euery shires end
Of engelond to caunterbury they wende
The holy blissefull martir for to seke
That hem hath holpen whan þᵗat þey were seke
Byfille þat in that seson on a day
In southwerk atte tabbard as I lay
Redy to wend on my pilgrymage
To caunterbury / wᵗith full deuout courage
At niht was come into þat hostellerye
Well nyne ⁊and twentie on a company
Of sondry folk by aventure yfalle
In fellashipe ⁊and pilgrymes were they all
That towardes caunterbury wold ryde
The chambres ⁊and stables weren wyde
And well weren esed atte beste
⁊and schortlie whan þᵉ son / was to reste
So had I spoken wᵗith hem euerychone
That I was of here fellaschip a none
And made forwarde erly for to ryse
To take our wey there as I you deuise
But natheles whil I haue tyme ⁊and space
Or þat I ferther in tale pace
Me thinkeþ according to reason
To tell you all the condicion
Of ech of hem so as it semed me .
